import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/test_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: columns ['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type']
# index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: columns ['business_id', 'date', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# --- Transformation Plan ---
# Target schema: ['business_id': int, 'Score': float, 'date': int, 'type': str, 'ViolationTypeID': int, 'risk_category': str, 'description': str]
# Source0 has: business_id, Score, date, type
# Source1 has: business_id, date, ViolationTypeID, risk_category, description
#
# Join Source0 and Source1 on ['business_id', 'date'] because these columns exist in both and are keys.
# This join will combine Score and type from Source0 with ViolationTypeID, risk_category, description from Source1.
#
# After join, ensure data types match target schema.
# The join is an inner join to keep only matching records (common business_id and date).
#
# Finally, reorder columns to match target schema and write to CSV.

# Convert date columns to int if not already (some CSV readers may parse as int or str)
df0['date'] = df0['date'].astype(int)
df1['date'] = df1['date'].astype(int)

# Convert business_id to int (in case of float due to NaNs)
df0['business_id'] = df0['business_id'].astype(int)
df1['business_id'] = df1['business_id'].astype(int)

# Perform inner join on ['business_id', 'date']
df_merged = pd.merge(df0, df1, on=['business_id', 'date'], how='inner')

# Ensure columns have correct types as per target schema
df_merged['Score'] = df_merged['Score'].astype(float)  # Score is float, NaNs allowed
df_merged['type'] = df_merged['type'].astype(str)
df_merged['ViolationTypeID'] = df_merged['ViolationTypeID'].astype(int)
df_merged['risk_category'] = df_merged['risk_category'].astype(str)
df_merged['description'] = df_merged['description'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to target schema order
df_target = df_merged[['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']]

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
